The problem

The most expensive damage starts where you can't see it. VESTA puts sensors where water hides in every unit, your whole community on one live map, and a clear next step in your team's hands before it becomes a repair.

  • $13 billionYearly cost to insurers of non-weather water damage in U.S. commercial properties.1
  • 24–48 hoursFor mold to begin growing once materials stay wet.2
  • Limited visibilityMoisture builds up behind walls long before anyone can see it.

1. National Association of Insurance Commissioners, via Nationwide · 2. U.S. EPA

Platform

One quiet system that watches every room.

Sensors in each unit measure, and the VESTA app shows every reading in its place on a 3D model of the property. Your team hears from it when something needs them.

Book a portfolio demoSchedule a site assessment

Sensors

Two sensors, one for inside the wall, one for everywhere else.

Each sensor reports exactly what it measures, and nothing is filled in between rooms.

01 · 1.25 in (31.8 mm) cover plate

In-Wall Sensor

Detects hidden moisture risks before visible damage appears.

  • Placement: installed flush with the wall in high-risk areas
  • Monitoring: temperature and humidity inside the wall cavity and in the room
  • Additional detection: mVOC sensor for possible microbial activity

02 · 2.36 × 3.15 in (60 × 80 mm)

Stick-On Sensor

Simple protection for moisture-prone areas.

  • Placement: adhesive install under sinks, near plumbing or in utility spaces
  • Monitoring: surrounding temperature and humidity
  • Additional detection: mVOC sensing for possible microbial activity

Where sensors usually go in each unit

  • In-wall: walls behind kitchens, bathrooms and laundry, where plumbing runs
  • Stick-on: under sinks, beside water heaters and in utility spaces
  • Both: temperature, humidity and mVOC readings, room by room
  • Connected: sensors report over Bluetooth, so nothing needs wiring

Honest about gaps

If a sensor stops reporting, VESTA marks it offline on the site plan and in the alert feed, so a gap in data is never mistaken for an all-clear.

Digital twin

See the reading where it happens.

Every property in the portfolio gets a 3D model with each sensor at its mounted position. Start from a standard layout for each floor plan, or load a model from your architect or a scanning app (GLB or glTF).

Alerts

An alert you can act on.

Each alert names the unit and room, shows the reading and how long it has been out of range, and lists what to check first, so whoever picks it up knows exactly where to go. If the problem returns, it says when to call a plumber or other pro.

Check first

  1. Inspect the sink supply lines and drain behind this wall.
  2. Look for staining, bubbling paint or a musty smell.
  3. Dry it out within 24–48 hours to stay ahead of mold.

Why it matters

Fix the small problem on your schedule.

A rising reading in a basement wall is a work order you can plan. Found months later, it's a remediation project and an unhappy resident.

From reading to work order

Caught early, a leak stays small.

How a slow drip behind a kitchen wall plays out across your team with VESTA watching. Sample scenario.

  1. Monday, 6:10 AMHumidity starts climbing inside a kitchen wall in Unit 204.

    The in-wall sensor sees it rise while the room air stays normal. Nobody living there would notice yet.

  2. Monday, 12:10 PMVESTA alerts the property manager and maintenance.

    Building C turns amber on the site plan. The alert shows the wall on the unit's 3D model and lists what to check first.

  3. Monday, 3:00 PMA technician finds a loose supply line and fixes it.

    Well inside the 24–48 hour window before mold usually starts to grow.

  4. Next daysVESTA confirms the wall is drying.

    In-wall humidity and mVOC readings settle back to normal, and the alert is marked resolved in the activity feed.

FAQ

Questions, answered.

For property managers evaluating VESTA. Can't find what you need? Book a 15-minute call and ask us directly.

Getting started

Which properties is VESTA for?

Apartment complexes and multi-unit housing. We're starting in Oxford, Ohio, then expanding across Southwest Ohio and on to the Midwest, East Coast and West Coast.

What happens in a portfolio demo?

A 30-minute video call. We walk through the live site plan, a home's digital twin, the alert feed and reports on a sample community, then talk through your properties.

What is a site assessment?

An on-site visit to your community. We look at your home types and floor plans, plumbing runs, appliances, basements or crawlspaces and outside grading, then plan where sensors should go in each home.

Do residents need to be home?

Installation needs access to each home. We'll plan visits with your team so residents get notice the way you usually arrange maintenance access.

How quickly will you confirm my time?

The time you pick is a request. We confirm it by email, or suggest the nearest open time if that slot is taken.

The system

What do the sensors measure?

Both VESTA sensors track temperature and humidity and use an mVOC sensor to watch for possible microbial activity, an early sign of mold. The In-Wall Sensor also measures temperature and humidity inside the wall cavity through a vented probe, so it can catch moisture before any damage is visible.

How are the sensors installed?

The In-Wall Sensor installs flush with the wall in high-risk areas, behind a 1.25 in (31.8 mm) cover plate. The Stick-On Sensor (2.36 × 3.15 in) attaches with adhesive under sinks, near plumbing or in utility spaces. Both connect over Bluetooth.

What happens if a sensor goes offline?

VESTA marks it offline on the site plan, on the home's model and in the alert feed. Usually it needs to be reseated in its mount or is too far from the hub, and the app says which. Missing data is never shown as an all-clear.

Who gets the alerts?

You choose. Managers and maintenance staff can each get text, email or push for the alert types they handle. Routine notices respect quiet hours; critical alerts such as leaks always come through.

Can VESTA use 3D models of our actual floor plans?

Yes. We can start from a standard layout that matches each floor plan in your community, or load models from your architect or a scanning app (GLB or glTF). VESTA can't build a model from an address alone.

Portfolios

How many properties can we manage in VESTA?

The portfolio view is built for whole communities. Tell us about your portfolio when you book a demo, and we'll show it at that scale.

Can we export data?

Yes. Each property has an environmental report covering the last 90 days, and readings can be exported as CSV.
